sections.label: Vaporiser offender data Singapore
sections.summary: Passage states no local data exists on vaporiser use, but offender numbers rose from 2020 to 2021, suggesting increased use in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Currently, there is no available local data on the use of vaporisers as these are illegal products and reliable self-reported data is difficult to obtain.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: However, in 2021, there were 7,593 offenders, across all ages, caught for import of vaporisers, compared to 6,192 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Similarly, in 2021, there were a total of 4,697 offenders caught for purchase, use or possession of vaporisers, of which about one-third were under-18, compared to a total of 1,266 offenders in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: While data on number of offenders may not represent the total number of users, the trend does suggest a general increase in use of vaporisers in Singapore.

sections.label: Vape-free campaign for youths
sections.summary: The Health Promotion Board will roll out a vape-free campaign later in 2022 targeted at youths and younger adults through digital platforms.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Health Promotion Board will also roll out a vape-free campaign later in 2022 targeted at youths and younger adults through popular digital platforms.
